newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary says 1998 spending forecast excludes debt.
newsitem.headline: Hungary says 1998 spending forecast excludes debt.

text.p: The maximum 16 to 17 percent increase in expenditure of Hungary's 1998 government budget forecast by the government on Thursday excludes debt service requirements, Finance Ministry officials said on Friday.

Government spokesman Elemer Kiss said on Thursday that overall budget expenditures would rise by a maximum 16 to 17 percent, but Deputy State secretary Csaba Laszlo said Kiss had meant the primary government budget, which excludes debt service figures.
"This is the primary government budget," Laszlo told a news conference.

Department head Ferenc Batho added that the surplus of the primary government budget, including the central state budget, government funds and local municipalities, would drop to two percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1998 from 3.5 percent planned for 1997.
He said that part of the differential would finance the real value rise in expenditures.
The government forecasts inflation will average 13.5 percent next year.
Batho said the revenues of the primary budget are expected to increase by 10 to 12 percent in 1998 from 1997.
